bull.b: Robust operating and free cash flow gives T-Mobile meaningful internal funding for network investment, spectrum needs, debt service, and shareholder returns. Cash-backed earnings improve resilience and support strategic flexibility over the next several quarters.

Leading network performance and customer satisfaction can strengthen acquisition, retention, and share gains in a competitive wireless market. These advantages support pricing power and help make subscriber growth more durable than promotion-driven additions alone.

Reaffirmed service revenue growth alongside roughly 10% midpoint EBITDA growth indicates continued operating momentum and potential margin expansion. The quantified outlook provides a durable earnings framework supported by subscriber additions, ARPA growth, and recurring connectivity revenue.

bear.b: High leverage reduces financial flexibility and leaves more cash flow exposed to interest costs and refinancing needs. Declining equity while debt remains elevated could constrain investment, buybacks, or spectrum spending if operating conditions weaken.

bear.t: Planned Rate-Plan Modernization May Increase Churn
bear.b: Rate-plan modernization may disrupt customer relationships and slow account growth in the near term, particularly among fewer-line accounts. Even if temporary, higher churn can raise retention costs, dilute acquisition momentum, and pressure the reliability of subscriber forecasts.

SpaceX’s nationwide low-band spectrum acquisition could add a well-funded competitor with broader coverage ambitions to the U.S. wireless market. Over time, this may increase pressure on customer acquisition, network investment, pricing, and spectrum strategy for incumbent carriers.
